title: Legends live on in Nuevo Laredo's old cemetery on Day of the Dead
excerpt: On November 1, visitors to Nuevo Laredo's Antiguo Panteón Municipal walk among tombs that local lore has turned into living legends.
content:
On Day of the Dead, November 1, visitors to Nuevo Laredo's Antiguo Panteón Municipal walk among distinctive tombs that local lore has turned into living legends, according to El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo.

Among the tombs singled out are La Sirena, marked by a mermaid near the entrance and linked in local lore to a young woman who died in 1926; El Niño del Panteón, a child's tomb where visitors leave toys and other offerings and to which favors are attributed in local belief; and El Pirata, tied to a mysterious figure said to have arrived in 1910.

The account also names El Barón francés, a French baron figure said to have died in 1965 at age 73, along with the Tumba Amarilla and the Tumba Israelita, singled out for their unusual appearance and cultural and religious markers. Some sealed tombs are presented as especially mysterious.

These are stories passed down as local legend, not verified histories — part of how families mark Día de Muertos in the city's old cemetery, where the past is remembered tomb by tomb.

Sources:

  • El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo, "Tumbas diferentes son leyendas vivas en la historia de Nuevo Laredo," November 1, 2026
